what: the pinned x402 client packages, installed from the registry and run over every fixture in corpus/fixtures.json. Every outcome in this file was observed, not inferred
ran_is: carried forward unless --stamp is passed, so regenerating without changing an answer changes no bytes

install.method: first run resolves with `npm install` and records the lockfile; every later run installs it with `npm ci`
install.transitive_note: zod resolves transitively and its issue text is recorded verbatim, which is why the lockfile is committed rather than regenerated

exports.what: every subpath each package’s own exports map declares, imported, with its export names as they actually are

entry_points.name: core.utils.Base64EncodedRegex.test
entry_points.why: the gate decodePaymentRequiredHeader applies before it will look at the bytes at all

entry_points.name: core.http.decodePaymentRequiredHeader
entry_points.why: THE REAL DECODE PATH. Base64EncodedRegex test, then JSON.parse. No schema runs here

entry_points.name: core.http.x402HTTPClient#getPaymentRequiredResponse
entry_points.input: the recorded headers and the parsed body
entry_points.why: what a v2 client run actually executes: the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header if there is one, otherwise the body when it declares x402Version 1. This one method is where the two generations meet, so it is the entry point that answers "which path parsed this fixture"

entry_points.name: core.schemas.PaymentRequiredV2Schema.safeParse
entry_points.why: the exported schema. NOT called by the package on the payment path — a consumer has to reach for it. Where it disagrees with the decode path above, that disagreement is the finding

entry_points.name: core.schemas.PaymentRequiredSchema.safeParse
entry_points.why: the union a consumer reaches for when it does not already know which generation it holds

entry_points.name: core.schemas.PaymentRequirementsV2Schema.safeParse[]
entry_points.input: each entry of the decoded envelope’s accepts array
entry_points.why: per-offer, because an envelope with one good offer and one bad one is a different fact about interoperability than an envelope that fails whole

entry_points.name: core.schemas.PaymentRequiredV1Schema.safeParse
entry_points.why: the v2 package’s own view of a v1 body, which is what a dual-stack server is asking clients to accept

entry_points.name: x402.types.x402ResponseSchema.safeParse
entry_points.why: the v1 generation’s own envelope schema

entry_points.name: x402.types.PaymentRequirementsSchema.safeParse[]
entry_points.input: each entry of the body’s accepts array
entry_points.why: the schema x402-fetch calls with .parse() — the THROWING form — on every offer before it will select one. safeParse is used here only so every offer is reported instead of the first failure

entry_points.name: x402.client.selectPaymentRequirements
entry_points.why: v1 offer selection, which is pure and therefore reachable offline. Which offer a client would have picked is a PARSE-level fact; whether it could pay for it is not

entry_points.name: x402-fetch.wrapFetchWithPayment (response handling)
entry_points.input: the whole recorded response, served by a stub transport
entry_points.why: the v1 wrapper’s real 402 handling, run end to end up to the signing boundary. It calls PaymentRequirementsSchema.parse() — throwing, not safeParse — on every offer, so a single bad offer aborts the whole response. Selection is replaced by a recorder that THROWS a sentinel the moment it has chosen, which makes createPaymentHeader unreachable rather than merely unused

outcomes.accepted: the entry point returned; for a safeParse, success
outcomes.rejected: the entry point judged the input invalid — a zod failure or a documented validation throw
outcomes.threw: an error that is not one of the package’s documented refusals — a crash, not a declining. Never counted as a rejection
outcomes.n/a: the entry point’s input is absent from this fixture. Silence, not approval
outcomes.not-exercisable-offline: the path needs a key or a chain, and is recorded as a boundary rather than a result

not_exercisable_offline.reason: builds and signs an EIP-712 authorization; needs a private key. No key exists in this process

not_exercisable_offline.entry_point: @x402/evm exact/client, exact/v1/client, upto/client — payload construction and signing
not_exercisable_offline.reason: the signer. EVERY execute-level client_interop claim in this corpus cites this package, and none of them is observed here: signing needs a key, and settlement needs a chain
